action:
name: Setup pnpm with runtime
description: Install pnpm and a JavaScript runtime (Node.js, Bun, or Deno) in one step
branding:
  icon: package
  color: orange
inputs:
  version:
    description: |
      Version of pnpm to install: an exact version (`12.0.0`), a
      semver range (`^12.0.0`), or an npm dist-tag (`next-12`). Must resolve
      to pnpm v11 or newer — the action downloads pnpm's native per-platform
      executable directly, without needing Node.js or npm.

      When omitted, the version is read from `devEngines.packageManager` or
      `packageManager` in the project's package.json.
    required: false
  registry:
    description: |
      npm registry to resolve and download pnpm from, e.g. a mirror on a
      network that cannot reach registry.npmjs.org. Defaults to
      `https://registry.npmjs.org/`; registry environment variables such as
      `pnpm_config_registry` do not change it.

      The mirror has to proxy the npm registry rather than re-publish pnpm:
      the download is verified against npm's own signature, which it must
      pass through unchanged. This only affects how pnpm itself is fetched —
      configure pnpm's own `registry` setting, e.g. `pnpm_config_registry`,
      for `pnpm install`.
    required: false
  dest:
    description: |
      Where to store pnpm files. Also used as `PNPM_HOME`. The pnpm
      executable is kept in the runner's tool cache, reused when the same
      exact version is requested again, and linked into this directory.
    required: false
    default: ~/setup-pnpm
  runtime:
    description: |
      Runtime to install, in `<name>` or `<name>@<version>` form (matching
      pnpm's `packageManager` field syntax). Supported names: `node`, `bun`,
      `deno`. Examples: `node@22`, `node@lts`, `node@^24.4.0`, `bun@latest`,
      `deno@2`.

      When the version is omitted, the action falls back to the version
      declared in `devEngines.runtime` for the same name, or to `lts` (for
      `node`) / `latest` for others. For Node.js, an explicit version file
      overrides the manifest; automatically detected files are used after
      the manifest and before the `lts` fallback.

      If this input is omitted entirely, the action installs every runtime in
      `devEngines.runtime` from the project's package.json. In case of duplicates,
      the last declared version wins. Node.js is also installed when a
      version file supplies its version, unless an explicit Bun or Deno
      runtime was selected.

      Whenever a runtime is installed, the action exports
      `PNPM_CONFIG_GLOBAL_SHIMS` with that runtime's context-aware shim
      disabled, so later steps run exactly this version instead of one a
      project pins. Set the variable in the workflow to override.
    required: false
  node-version-file:
    description: |
      File containing the Node.js version to install, relative to
      `working-directory`. When omitted, automatically checks `.node-version`,
      `.nvmrc`, then `.tool-versions` if no Node.js version is declared in
      `devEngines.runtime`. Set to `false` to disable version-file detection.
      An explicit file path takes precedence over `devEngines.runtime`.

      When `runtime` is omitted, this installs Node.js alongside any non-Node
      runtimes declared in `devEngines.runtime`. A version included directly
      in `runtime` takes precedence, and an explicit Bun or Deno runtime
      ignores version files. `.tool-versions` uses the first version in its
      `node` or `nodejs` entry; automatic detection ignores it without that entry.
    required: false
  cache:
    description: |
      Whether to cache the pnpm store directory, keyed on the lockfile's
      content hash, and restore it before installing the runtimes. When the
      pnpm version is exact, the pnpm executable is cached too. The results
      of pnpm's lockfile verification are cached either way — see the README.
    required: false
    default: 'false'
  save-cache:
    description: |
      Whether to save the pnpm store at the end of the job when `cache` is
      `true`. Set to `false` to only restore it, for example in jobs that
      should not write to the cache. The lockfile verification cache is
      saved either way.
    required: false
    default: 'true'
  cache-dependency-path:
    description: |
      File path to the pnpm lockfile, whose contents hash is used as a cache
      key. Relative to the repository root (GITHUB_WORKSPACE). Defaults to
      the shared workspace lockfile for workspace members, or `pnpm-lock.yaml`
      inside `working-directory` for standalone and per-project installs.
    required: false
  working-directory:
    description: |
      Directory the project lives in, relative to the repository root
      (GITHUB_WORKSPACE). The action runs `pnpm install` there and resolves
      `node-version-file` relative to it. For workspace members, package-manager
      selection and shared-lockfile caching follow the workspace root.
      Defaults to the repository root.

      pnpm finds the workspace root itself by walking up, so a project
      inside a pnpm workspace does not need this — point it at a project
      whose root is not the repository root.
    required: false
    default: '.'
  package-json-file:
    description: |
      Deprecated. Use `working-directory` instead: the manifest is read
      from that directory, which is also where `pnpm install` runs. Still
      honoured when set on its own — the directory containing the file
      becomes the working directory.
    required: false
    deprecationMessage: 'The package-json-file input is deprecated; use working-directory instead.'
  require-lockfile:
    description: |
      Whether the install has to be fully described by `pnpm-lock.yaml`.

      When `true`, the action fails if no lockfile is found — in
      `working-directory` or, as pnpm itself searches, above it — without
      running pnpm at all, and otherwise runs the install with
      `--frozen-lockfile`.

      This is narrower than it sounds. pnpm already refuses to update an
      *existing* lockfile when it detects CI, and GitHub Actions always sets
      `CI`, so an out-of-date lockfile fails a plain install anyway. What that
      default does not do is require a lockfile to exist: with none at all,
      `pnpm install` resolves from the registry, writes one and exits 0. Set
      this when that should fail the job instead.
    required: false
    default: 'false'
  install:
    description: |
      Whether to run `pnpm install` after pnpm and the runtime are set up.

      When set to `true` (the default), the action runs `pnpm install` in the
      workspace when a package.json is present. When runtimes are installed,
      `--no-runtime` is appended automatically because the action has already
      processed `devEngines.runtime`.

      Set to `false` to skip the install step — useful for jobs that only
      need pnpm itself (e.g. `pnpm audit`, lockfile-only regeneration).
    required: false
    default: 'true'
  token:
    description: >
      No longer used. pnpm is fetched from the npm registry and verified
      against npm's signature, so no GitHub API request is made. Kept so
      workflows that pass it keep working.
    required: false
    deprecationMessage: 'The token input is no longer used; pnpm is fetched from the npm registry.'

outputs:
  dest:
    description: Expanded path of inputs#dest
  bin-dest:
    description: Location of `pnpm` and `pnpx` command
  runtime-name:
    description: Name of the first installed runtime (`node`, `bun`, or `deno`), or empty if none was installed
  runtime-version:
    description: Resolved version of the first installed runtime, or empty if none was installed
  runtimes:
    description: JSON array of installed runtimes, each containing `name` and `version`
  cache-hit:
    description: Whether the restored cache matched the current lockfile exactly, rather than falling back to a store cached for a different lockfile
runs:
  using: node24
  main: dist/index.js
  post: dist/index.js
